(3) The closing whole-document rebuild still costs one ~83 ms hitch at the end of a reply.
- Headings scale off the base font size, so `MarkdownBlock` rebuilds its document when `FontSize` changes — the scaled sizes are baked into the document and would otherwise keep the previous scale.

-- Links are real `Hyperlink`s (v262.0; previously coloured runs with custom click hit-testing): `FlowDocumentScrollViewer` has no public text hit-test API, so `BuildLink` stamps the URL onto `Hyperlink.Tag` and `MarkdownBlock` handles `Hyperlink.Click` (with `handledEventsToo`) and raises `LinkClicked`. `MarkdownBlock.LinkClicked` bubbles through `ChatTranscriptView.LinkClicked` (wired on every `MarkdownBlock` instance — the assistant body, the thinking block, the plan-review card and, since v181.0, the notice and error rows) to `OnChatLinkClicked` in `NativeChat.cs`, which opens `http`/`https` URLs with `Process.Start(UseShellExecute: true)` and treats everything else as a file reference, splitting a trailing `:line` or `:line-line2` (`ChatFileLineRefPattern`, greedy so a Windows drive-letter colon does not get mistaken for the split point) and resolving the path via `ResolveChatFileLinkAsync` — tried as typed, then joined to the workspace root, then matched by trailing segment/filename against the same `_atEntries` index the `@`-mention picker builds (agents often cite a bare filename or a path relative to a different root). A match opens through `EnvDTE.DTE.ItemOperations.OpenFile` + `TextSelection.GotoLine`, the same mechanism `DiffViewerControl.OpenFileInEditor` uses.

Links are `Focusable = false` (v293.0, #250): a `Hyperlink` focuses itself on mouse down, and the focus raises `RequestBringIntoView` up to the virtualized transcript's `ScrollViewer`, which scrolled a reader who had scrolled back away from the clicked answer before the click landed, so the file only opened on the second click. `MarkdownBlock.LinkClicked` bubbles through `ChatTranscriptView.LinkClicked` (wired on every `MarkdownBlock` instance — the assistant body, the thinking block, the plan-review card and, since v181.0, the notice and error rows) to `OnChatLinkClicked` in `NativeChat.cs`, which opens `http`/`https` URLs with `Process.Start(UseShellExecute: true)` and treats everything else as a file reference, splitting a trailing `:line` or `:line-line2` (`ChatFileLineRefPattern`, greedy so a Windows drive-letter colon does not get mistaken for the split point) and resolving the path via `ResolveChatFileLinkAsync` — tried as typed, then joined to the workspace root, then matched by trailing segment/filename against the same `_atEntries` index the `@`-mention picker builds (agents often cite a bare filename or a path relative to a different root). A match opens through `EnvDTE.DTE.ItemOperations.OpenFile` + `TextSelection.GotoLine`, the same mechanism `DiffViewerControl.OpenFileInEditor` uses.

- Bare URLs and file citations are auto-linked too (v107.0), not just `[label](url)` syntax — measured against a real turn, agents asked for `file.cs:41`-style citations wrote plain text with no brackets around it far more often than markdown links. `AppendInlines` matches `AutoUrlPattern` (`https?://…`, trimmed of trailing sentence punctuation via `TrimTrailingPunctuation`) and `AutoFileRefPattern` (`path/File.ext:123` or `:123-456`, requiring a dot-plus-extension before the colon so "ratio 3:1" or a "10:41" timestamp is never mistaken for a citation) at every `h`/word-start character, and routes a hit through the same `BuildLink` as an explicit link. Bracketed links are matched first (the `[` branch runs before the autolink checks) so nothing double-processes.

- Citations wrapped in a code span are auto-linked too (v108.0): agents just as often write `` `Program.cs:56` `` or wrap a whole line — `` `Program.cs:56 — public async Task Foo()` `` — as one inline-code span, which used to render as a single flat `Run` with `CodeBackground` and no `Tag`, so nothing inside a backtick span was ever clickable. The backtick branch in `AppendInlines` now delegates to `AppendCodeSpanInlines`, which re-runs the same `AutoUrlPattern`/`AutoFileRefPattern` scan over the span's contents: a matched segment becomes a link (`BuildLink`, monospace font kept, no `CodeBackground` — so it reads as a link, not an inert code block) and everything around it keeps the normal monospace-plus-background code styling.

- Selection uses `ChatSelectionBrush`, not the VS theme's `HighlightKey` (v107.0): the theme highlight renders as a saturated violet block in the transcript and fights with the accent-blue link text sitting on it. `MarkdownBodyStyle` (assistant replies, user messages, notices/errors) and `ChatToolTextStyle` (tool input/result) use a translucent tint of `ChatAccentBrush` instead (`#661C8AE0`, with `SelectionOpacity="1"` so the brush's own alpha is the only transparency in play). The composer input and the interaction cards' free-text answer box keep the VS highlight — those are real editable text, where matching the rest of Visual Studio is correct.

content.text:
I fixed and published #250 as version 293.0.

**#250: Native chat code citation jumps to the latest answer on the first click** (reported by @fanyu99)
- **The problem:** if you had scrolled back in a long chat, the first click on a file reference moved the chat to a recent answer. The file only opened on a second click.
- **The cause:** the reporter's analysis was right. A chat link takes keyboard focus when you press the mouse on it, and that focus makes the chat scroll before the click is handled.
- **The fix:** chat links no longer take keyboard focus. It's a one-line change in `UI/MarkdownFlowRenderer.cs`. The same code draws links in the GitHub Issues window, so those get the fix too. One trade-off: you can no longer reach links with the Tab key.
- **Also in the change:** a new unit test, a note in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, the version bump to 293.0, and a README entry crediting @fanyu99.
- **Checks:** the Release build and all 1041 tests passed, and `publish.cmd` reported a successful upload. I pushed commit `8f98914`.
- **Not tested in Visual Studio:** I didn't try it by hand. The reporter says they tested the same change in the experimental instance.
- **The issue:** "Fixes #250" in the commit closed it when I pushed, and I posted a thank-you reply describing the fix.

Nothing in the issue looked suspicious.
